verdict.rationale: Gmail's documented delegation lets one or more delegates read, send and delete mail in a shared account, so a team can work the same mailbox and conversation state. That covers the shared-account half of the story. Nothing in the evidence shows team-inbox features such as team channels, assignment or collision detection. Missing for 10: purpose-built shared or team inbox or channel features, documentation that delegates see synchronized read/conversation state, independent corroboration of team use.

support.subject: As a team-lead, my team works shared inboxes together — shared accounts or team channels where everyone sees the same conversation state

citations.quote: You can grant one or more delegates access to your Gmail account. A delegate is someone who can read, send, and delete emails in your account for you.
Delegates can read, send, and delete messages, as well as view and add contacts on behalf of the delegator's account.
